status: draft: written and dry-run on development cases only; not frozen, not run
question: When independent task authors correct a robot task specification in their own words, across new scenes, object scopes and multi-turn changes, how often does MIRROR (Muse Spark compiling corrections) produce the intended specification and a compliant execution, compared with the offline rule compiler and with manual structured-spec editing, all through an identical planner, simulator and checker?

layers.authoring: text or speech -> TaskSpec version (scored against an adjudicated gold edit)
layers.execution: authored TaskSpec -> plan -> MuJoCo -> checker under the gold TaskSpec
layers.perception: not in this protocol; demonstration traces are the simulator's (reported separately by the video and robustness registrations)
layers.composition: end-to-end success per case = authoring then execution on the same case

mirror_model.speech: spoken turns transcribed by muse-voice-transcribe-1.0 (PUSH_TO_TALK), transcript compiled

manual_structured.editor: an independent editor (not the case author, not the adjudicator) enters a StructuredEdit per turn from the turn text and the scene description, without seeing the gold
manual_structured.time: editor's own measured seconds per turn (reported; authoring time is the impact study's endpoint, not this protocol's)

cases.authors: 5-8 independent authors (robotics engineers or integrators), none of whom wrote MIRROR's compiler, prompts or earlier benchmarks
cases.per_author: 15 cases; at least 3 multi-turn; categories in the proportions below
must_cover: new wording (no sentence from the earlier benchmark or prompts; checked by word-bigram overlap before the freeze, overlapping cases flagged and scored separately)
object scopes cup, block, marker and every object
reversals and exceptions in later turns
spoken turns by real speakers (consented), never mixed with synthetic speech

scenes.sampled: assigned by the custodian at freeze from reserved seed ranges

cases.gold: each turn adjudicated by two people who did not author the case; disagreements resolved before the freeze and recorded; ambiguous and unsupported turns have gold asks/rejects
cases.manual_edits: collected from editors before the freeze; an empty edit means the editor declined to change the spec

access.dev: mirror/evaluate/protocol_v3/dev_cases.json, team-written, dev seeds 9600-9699 and reference scenes; used to build and debug the harness
access.holdout: bundle held by a custodian outside the repository; freeze manifest commits to its sha256, case-id hash, count per author and per category; loader refuses a bundle inside the repository before the run finishes or one that does not match the commitment; committed to results/protocol_v3/ only after the run
access.submission: authors fill the packet in docs/protocols/v3_author_packet.md and send it to the custodian only; developers receive hashes and counts, never text, until the run has finished

seeds.check: no earlier ledger contains any reserved seed (verified 2026-11-02: largest recorded evaluation seed 80007)

turn: exact (outcome and semantic enforced state equal gold)
wrong-scope edit (changed an object kind the gold turn did not)
case: end-to-end success: compliant_completion = rollout of the authored spec passes the checker under the gold spec; proven_infeasible = the planner stops with a proof; unknown when any requirement could not be verified (never success)
planning time, simulated execution time, path length, routes
metrics.old_behaviour: base-spec rollout on each scene re-checked under the gold spec (independent rejection of the old behaviour)

scoring_notes: semantic comparison: an every-object rule equals the same rule on each object kind (unlike the earlier benchmark's strict id match)
a manual abstention on an ambiguous or unsupported turn counts as a refusal of unspecified type
replay without a recording is 'not measured', excluded and listed, never replaced by another interpreter

analysis.primary: case-level end-to-end success, mirror_model vs offline_rules and mirror_model vs manual_structured, exact McNemar (two-sided), unknown cases excluded and counted
secondary: turn exact, false accepts, wrong-scope turns per condition with Wilson intervals
spoken (real speakers) vs typed for mirror_model
analysis.disclosure: these thresholds were written after a dry run on the team's 18 development cases; the dev numbers are reported with the protocol

every_attempt: attempts.jsonl records a start and an end line per case x condition; statuses completed, timeout, error, budget_stopped, interrupted; nothing is filtered by outcome
amendments: none allowed after the freeze; a change after any failure creates protocol version 3.1 with a new manifest, new seeds and a new held-out bundle

jobs.what: record Muse Spark on the 18 development cases so the mirror_model dry run is measured end to end
jobs.calls: <= 22 compile_correction requests (+ repair retries <= 2 each) to muse-spark-1.3
<= 250 turns x <= 3 attempts of compile_correction to muse-spark-1.3; <= 120 real-speaker clips (<= 15 min audio) to muse-voice-transcribe-1.0
jobs.compute: CPU only, about 400 simulated executions at about 5 s each

prerequisites: recruited independent authors, editors, adjudicators and real speakers with signed consent (study/consent_form.md)
a custodian who is not a developer
freeze committed before the bundle is opened
